transactional-crm.name: CRM & AI workflow integration
transactional-crm.problem: Customer-service teams need workflows shaped around their own follow-up, analysis and approval problems. A useful CRM must connect business context with the next action.
transactional-crm.role: I designed and built the CRM, API and CLI as a customisable foundation for AI-assisted service workflows, linking customer history, projects, invoices and versioned notes.
transactional-crm.decision: My integration approach is to connect reminders and business analysis to proposed actions, with human approval before consequential execution. Stable request keys, version checks and attributed updates make agent writes traceable and protect shared records.
transactional-crm.evidence: The internal system includes follow-up reminders, shared business records and controlled API/CLI writes. Broader AI analysis and decision workflows are extension areas tailored to each business. The fictional-data demo shows the implemented write-safety rules.

bookkeeping-assistant.name: NZ Accounting Assistant
bookkeeping-assistant.problem: Receipts and bank statements arrive in different formats. Preparing a reviewable ledger requires matching entries without losing the original evidence.
bookkeeping-assistant.role: I built the reusable skill and supporting tooling for evidence capture, ledger preparation, reconciliation and export.
bookkeeping-assistant.decision: Unclear matches must remain visible. Preserve source files, normalise records into JSON and leave ambiguous items for human confirmation before preparing exports.
bookkeeping-assistant.evidence: Public workflow instructions and scripts cover Xero CSV exports and accountant review packs. Financial records and final decisions remain subject to human review.

voice-companion.name: HiLily
voice-companion.problem: Hardware development and extending it into a complete software system are central challenges for this voice companion, especially echo, noisy environments and conversational response time.
voice-companion.role: As a volunteer AI Coach, I contribute technical guidance on the hardware-to-software AI pipeline, microphone audio processing and low-latency speech-to-speech model integration. Hardware and product delivery are team efforts.
voice-companion.decision: The work includes echo cancellation with single- and dual-microphone setups, recognition in noisy environments, and audio-in/audio-out language models. I help the team work through these connected constraints across device audio, model integration and system extension.
voice-companion.evidence: The project website includes demonstrations and my team role. The team reports a working MVP with multiple iterations completed and is preparing for real-world pilots.

codexview.name: CodexView
codexview.problem: Coding agents produce different transcript formats. Reviewing tool calls and nested sessions should not require a different viewer for every agent.
codexview.role: I developed the transcript adapters, React components and Markdown CLI as reusable packages.
codexview.decision: Keep format parsing separate from presentation. Adapters produce a shared event model that supports both a visual transcript and compact text, preserving tool and subagent context.
codexview.evidence: The public repository contains the three packages, usage examples and test fixtures. The implementation can be inspected independently of private workbench projects.

crmDemo.title: One record. Two editors. A visible history.
crmDemo.label: CRM workflow demonstration
crmDemo.intro: Fictional data, running only in your browser. This simplified simulation illustrates the implemented request and version rules; it does not connect to the private CRM or reproduce its production interface.
crmDemo.storyTitle: Building AI workflows around the service problem
story: I use the CRM with a colleague for internal customer-service work. The design starts with practical questions: who needs a follow-up, what business context informs the next action, and who should approve it.

I built a shared data model, API and CLI around customer relationships, projects, invoices and versioned notes. Follow-up reminders are implemented. These provide the context and controlled write path for business-specific AI workflows.

The integration pattern is reminder or business event, contextual analysis, proposed action, human review, execution and a recorded result. Broader AI analysis and decision flows are extension areas; their rules and approval points must be tailored to the actual service process.
Make the workflow safe to operate

People retain approval of consequential actions. Version checks reject stale edits, retries do not create duplicate records, and note history preserves prior content. The next iteration should be driven by real usage and unresolved cases; no measured productivity gain or external adoption is claimed.
details: Create one fictional record with request key demo-note-001.
Resend the identical request and key: return the original record without creating a second one.
A colleague adds a review requirement. The saved record becomes version 2.
The agent still holds version 1. Reject its edit with 409 and preserve the colleague’s change.
A person reads version 2 and combines both changes. Saving with the current version creates version 3.
notes: Prepare the project brief. Include a review meeting.
Prepare the project brief. Include a review meeting and an evidence checklist.
outcomes: Ready. Start by creating a fictional note.
Replay: same record ID, one note, version 1.
200 OK: colleague’s update saved as version 2.
409 Conflict: stale edit rejected; version 2 is unchanged.
200 OK: reviewed merge saved as version 3.
